bull_case: Axon improves with conversion data while MAX expands publisher auction access, creating a reinforcing demand-data-supply loop. Better ROI attracts spend, generating more data and stronger monetization across the platform.
bear_case: The feedback loop can be weakened by privacy limits, platform data restrictions or better models from Meta/Google/Amazon. Advertisers can multi-home and shift budgets, so switching costs are economic rather than contractual.
thesis: APP's moat is widening through data/model feedback, publisher monetization infrastructure and advertiser performance rather than hard lock-in. High growth with rising margins suggests the flywheel is strengthening. MAX, Adjust and Wurl add workflow and distribution depth around Axon. The moat is not invulnerable: advertisers multi-home, Apple/Google control key ecosystem rules, and hyperscale platforms have larger first-party data pools.

evidence.claim: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 82.3% from 74.8% while revenue grew 70%, consistent with strong scale economics.
H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 84.2% while revenue grew 56%.
The product stack combines AppLovin Ads, MAX, Adjust and Wurl, integrating demand, publisher monetization, measurement and CTV distribution.
Management continues investing in Axon model enhancements and new verticals.

counterevidence: Advertisers can multi-home across ad platforms with relatively low contractual switching cost.
Apple and Google can restrict identifiers and attribution data.
Meta/Google/Amazon possess enormous first-party datasets and distribution.
Independent adtech historically faces commoditization and take-rate pressure.
unknowns: Relative conversion lift from Axon over peers.
Publisher share and retention for MAX.
Impact of future privacy APIs on model performance.

uncertainties.rationale: Economic performance creates stickiness, but direct pricing power and switching costs are not disclosed.
Growth and margin evidence strongly support a reinforcing data/scale loop.
Platform policy and hyperscale competitors can compress differentiation.

falsifiers: Revenue growth decelerates while digital-ad market remains strong and competitors gain share.
Margins fall structurally as take rates compress or data costs rise.
Platform/privacy changes materially weaken Axon performance.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Current growth, margins and product expansion indicate a strengthening rather than persistently shrinking moat.

key_kpis.name: Platform-policy impact
key_kpis.threshold: No sustained degradation in targeting economics

subscores.rationale: ROI-driven budget stickiness is strengthening despite easy multi-homing.
Demand, publisher inventory and conversion data reinforce Axon model performance.
Integrated stack defends differentiation, but platform and hyperscale competition remain serious.
